text:
sarah: Quick heads-up — SOC asked for a change to how we export security logs to the SIEM. They need 90d of full-fidelity logs for investigations, but dev teams only want masked fields for day-to-day debugging. How do we want to model this in retention + RBAC?

jamal: Do we have precedent? I thought we kept 30d raw + 1y masked in S3 lifecycle.

sarah: Right now infra lifecycle is 30d raw -> 365d archive, but the raw data is encrypted with CMK that limits who can decrypt (KMS). SOC wants direct access from Splunk -> needs decryption permissions.

li: We should avoid granting cross-team decrypt on the CMK. Proposal: keep raw in a SOC-only bucket with a KMS key that has a dedicated key policy and a small reader role for SOC. Devs get a masked view via a separate export feed.

maria: +1. Also recommend we implement masking at the producer side (log forwarder) so masked artifacts never land in dev-access buckets. Easier for compliance audits.

paul: For incident response we sometimes need elevated access. Suggest an "ephemeral-unmask" workflow: SOC can request a time-limited IAM role that can decrypt and is audited. Approvals go through PagerDuty or a ticket.

sarah: That fits. Questions: 1) lifecycle rules for the SOC bucket? 2) how to enforce and log ephemeral roles? 3) SIEM export config — Splunk needs access pattern.

jamal: Lifecycle: keep raw for 90d warm, then move to cold S3-IA with 2yr retention before delete. Example rule: 
```
{
  "Rules": [
    {"ID":"raw-soc-90d", "Prefix":"", "Status":"Enabled", "Transitions":[{"Days":90,"StorageClass":"STANDARD_IA"}], "Expiration":{"Days":730}}
  ]
}
```
This keeps it for 2 yrs total. 

li: For ephemeral roles: we already have an AWS STS approver flow for oncall. We can reuse that. Need to add KMS:GrantCreate + GrantConstraints so the grant auto-expires. Also wire CloudTrail events to a separate audit index.

maria: Masking rules idea: redwood-logforwarder config snippet: 
```yaml
filters:
  - field: user_email
    action: mask
    pattern: "*@redwood.com"
  - field: credit_card
    action: drop
```
Masked feed exports to bucket "redwood-logs-masked" with 1y retention.

paul: For Splunk/SIEM: best to use a read-only service role that assumes role into S3 and reads objects. Service role only has kms:Decrypt on SOC CMK. For masked exports we give read-only on masked bucket without decrypt.

sarah: Are there any objections to creating a dedicated SOC CMK (alias/aws/redwood-soc-logs) and a SOC-only bucket? We'll add an automated grant workflow for incidents.

jamal: No objections. One caveat: billing and egress. If Splunk pulls a lot, we need to route through VPC endpoints to avoid public egress charges.

maria: Also we should update our runbook and the audit playbook: include sample CloudTrail query to show who created/deleted grants and who assumed ephemeral roles.

li: I'll draft the KMS key policy and the IAM role trust policy. Will include condition for aws:SourceIp and mfa.

sarah: Great. Action items: li -> KMS key policy + grant workflow PR; jamal -> S3 lifecycle + VPC endpoint cost estimate; maria -> update runbooks + masking rules; paul -> add ephemeral approver into PD rotation. I'll own the SIEM export config.

sec-bot: New incident playbook update required: https://docs.internal/redwood/security/log-access-playbook (stub created) :eyes:

paul: Thanks — timeline?

li: Will open PR by EOD Thur (1868090000).

jamal: I'll have lifecycle + cost numbers by next Tue.

maria: Runbook draft in a docs PR by next Wed.

sarah: Nice. If anyone runs into permission gating, ping me and I'll escalate.

paul: Approved, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
